title: Issue #179: catalog: define X34 resource scheduling, capacity allocation and workload governance contracts
content:
State: open

## X34 – Ecosystem Resource Scheduling, Capacity Allocation & Workload Governance

**Architecture-ID:** `ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X34-RESOURCE-SCHEDULING-CAPACITY-ALLOCATION-WORKLOAD-GOVERNANCE`  
**Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`  
**Planned scope:** 17 sublayers / 170 function contracts (`X34-001`–`X34-170`)

## Goal and scope

Define governance contracts for planning, allocation, prioritization, reservation, and monitoring of resources and workloads across A-TownChain, GlobusOS, ShivaCore, Aurora AI, build/test workloads, and explicitly registered external compute providers.

X34 is an architecture/catalog/integration/evidence layer. It must **not** introduce a second scheduler, resource manager, kernel resource-management implementation, blockchain scheduler, or AI runtime. Existing canonical implementations remain authoritative.

### Boundaries
- **X8:** performance, capacity and resource optimization.
- **X12:** resource governance, cost control and economic sustainability.
- **X14:** runtime configuration and environment governance.
- **X34:** reservations, workload scheduling decisions, fairness, admission control and capacity limits.

## Planned sublayers and function-contract ranges

Each item below is a planning index only. Listing does not prove catalog intake, implementation, or verification.

1. **X34.01 – Resource Inventory & Capability Discovery** (`X34-001`–`X34-010`): resource classes; CPU/GPU/NPU, memory and storage inventory; hardware capabilities; canonical component identity; availability versus reservation; metadata versioning; untrusted-description validation; stale-resource marking; inventory evidence.
2. **X34.02 – Workload Classification & Execution Profiles** (`X34-011`–`X34-020`): workload type; compute/I/O and persistence requirements; runtime/deadline; interactive/batch/background classes; trust/isolation; profile versioning; reject unsupported profiles; map requirements to capabilities; record execution deviations.
3. **X34.03 – Scheduling Policy & Decision Governance** (`X34-021`–`X34-030`): register strategies; declarative rules; explain decisions; record policy version/time; block unauthorized changes; deterministic modes where required; detect infeasible workloads; resolve/escalate conflicts; authorized manual overrides; auditable decision logs.
4. **X34.04 – Capacity Planning & Admission Control** (`X34-031`–`X34-040`): budgets; pre-admission checks; bounded explicit overcommit; critical-service reserves; forecasts with uncertainty; reject infeasible work; recheck capacity on changes; distinguish planned from available capacity; explain admission; escalate shortages.
5. **X34.05 – Priority, Fairness & Starvation Prevention** (`X34-041`–`X34-050`): priority classes; tenant/service fairness; detect starvation; aging or equivalent protection; critical-service priority; bound escalation; prevent self-assigned priority abuse; evaluate cross-resource fairness; audit priority changes; measurable violation reporting.
6. **X34.06 – Resource Reservation & Lease Management** (`X34-051`–`X34-060`): unique reservations; scope/lease duration; expiry/renewal; duplicate/conflicting reservations; bind to authorized workloads; orphan cleanup; safe release; restart recovery; atomic changes within SSOT boundaries; audit reservation lifecycle.
7. **X34.07 – CPU, Memory & Compute Scheduling** (`X34-061`–`X34-070`): CPU budgets; memory limits; parallelism; overload/memory pressure; contention; policy-bound CPU affinity; hardware matching; controlled exhaustion handling; reconcile allocations with runtime measurements; protect limits against bypass.
8. **X34.08 – GPU, NPU & Accelerator Allocation** (`X34-071`–`X34-080`): capabilities/drivers; accelerator requirements; assignment versus sharing; authorized device access; accelerator-memory limits; reject incompatible models/devices; device-loss handling; restart recovery; comparable measurements; document device-specific isolation.
9. **X34.09 – Storage, I/O & Network Resource Scheduling** (`X34-081`–`X34-090`): storage/I/O budgets; latency; network bandwidth; critical-path reservations; queue/pressure monitoring; quotas; temporary versus persistent data; overload control; transparent throttling/rejection; bind allocation to privacy/access policies.
10. **X34.10 – Isolation, Tenancy & Resource Boundaries** (`X34-091`–`X34-100`): tenant/security-domain resource boundaries; capability limits; prevent cross-workload leaks; separate privileged resources; delegate isolation to canonical runtime; block unauthorized allocation; trace cross-tenant occupancy; preserve isolation during rescheduling; record violations; test/evidence isolation.
11. **X34.11 – Deadline, Latency & Real-Time Constraints** (`X34-101`–`X34-110`): deadlines/time budgets; hard versus soft real-time; scheduling latency; detect infeasible deadlines; report misses; validated priority for time-critical services; coordinate dependent workflows; safe timeout handling; latency distributions/percentiles; claim guarantees only with platform evidence.
12. **X34.12 – AI Workload & Model Inference Scheduling** (`X34-111`–`X34-120`): LLM/SLM/vision/embedding classes; map models to local hardware; context/batch/memory budgets; separate interactive/background inference; policy-based local/external routing; cost and data-transfer constraints; cancellation/preemption; backend failure; distinguish tool calls from inference; audit without disclosing prompts or user data.
13. **X34.13 – Blockchain, VM & Validator Resource Budgets** (`X34-121`–`X34-130`): classify node workloads; isolate consensus/validator resources; align VM budgets with canonical rules; validate transaction limits; separate block processing/background tasks; node network/storage needs; prevent unauthorized protocol-limit changes; monitor validator overload; label unfinalized protocol assumptions; check against canonical protocol/VM specs.
14. **X34.14 – Distributed Scheduling & Federation** (`X34-131`–`X34-140`): register providers; verify provenance/trust; declare node boundaries; distinguish commitments from forecasts; prevent double allocation; handle stale offers/disconnections; govern migration/rescheduling; enforce locality/data-residency policy; record provenance; safe behavior under partitions/unreachable providers.
15. **X34.15 – Autoscaling, Adaptation & Load Shedding** (`X34-141`–`X34-150`): triggers/thresholds; capacity-bound scaling; detect oscillation; controlled load shedding; defer noncritical work; preserve critical minimums; account for warm-up delays; policy-bound automation; controlled resumption; measure effects/side effects.
16. **X34.16 – Resource Accounting, Quotas & Allocation Evidence** (`X34-151`–`X34-160`): measure consumption; distinguish requested/reserved/used; quotas by service/tenant/security domain; classify quota violations; link cost policy; validate measurements; link allocation to policy and decision; mark incomplete usage data; unique run/artifact references; reproducible export.
17. **X34.17 – Scheduler Conformance, Testing & Lifecycle** (`X34-161`–`X34-170`): conformance tests; races; exhaustion/overload simulation; measurable fairness/starvation tests; release/restart recovery tests; hardware/backend compatibility; adversarial isolation tests; Run/Job/Step evidence with exit codes/logs; catalog exact repo/SHA/path/symbol; version/migrate/deprecate contracts.

## Proposed data contract (not normative)

Proposed convention: `ATC-WORKLOAD-CONTRACT-V1`. This is not yet a registered `atc-standards` standard.

```yaml
contract_id: ATC-WORKLOAD-CONTRACT-V1
schema_version: 1

workload:
  workload_id: required
  workload_type: required
  owner_identity: required
  execution_profile_ref: required
  priority_class: required
  deadline: optional

resources:
  cpu_budget: conditional
  memory_budget: conditional
  accelerator_profile: conditional
  storage_budget: conditional
  network_budget: conditional
  max_parallelism: required

allocation:
  reservation_id: optional
  allocation_policy_ref: required
  isolation_profile_ref: required
  quota_scope: required
  lease_expiry: conditional

security:
  capability_ref: required
  data_classification: required
  approval_ref: conditional

lifecycle:
  state: required
  retry_policy_ref: required
  cancellation_policy_ref: required
  completion_evidence_ref: conditional

rules:
  invalid_profile: reject
  unauthorized_allocation: reject
  capacity_exceeded: reject_or_defer
  expired_lease: reclaim_only_after_safe_release
  missing_evidence: not_verified
```

Before standardization, replace placeholders with concrete data types, units, time semantics, error codes and normative validation rules.

## SSOT and ownership

- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: architecture, integration, catalog, compliance, evidence and drift control only.
- `atc-standards`: normative resource/workload contracts only after formal registration and versioning.
- `a-townchain`: canonical blockchain node/protocol resources.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical ATC-VM execution and gas/resource limits.
- `a-townchain/components/algorithm`: canonical consensus/algorithm requirements.
- `globus-os/modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/`: canonical kernel resource management.
- `globus-os`: OS services, desktop and platform integration according to actual module paths.
- Aurora AI: verify canonical Aurora/runtime repository and paths before catalog mapping.
- Build/CI workloads: each canonical build and CI configuration.
- External compute: explicitly registered adapters with trust and resource boundaries.
- `demo-repository` remains excluded from the live drift gate.

Unknown ownership or paths must remain `UNRESOLVED` until evidenced. X34 must not create duplicate implementations or override canonical VM/protocol limits.

## Required invariants

- Every privileged allocation is policy-authorized; workload self-classification cannot grant privileges.
- Forecast capacity, currently available capacity, reservations, and allocated capacity are distinct.
- Security/capability/isolation boundaries take precedence over fairness.
- Overcommit is permitted only by explicit policy with measurable bounds and defined failure semantics.
- A timeout alone does not prove a process or external operation has stopped; release only after safe release is established.
- Real-time, hardware-isolation and accelerator guarantees require platform evidence.
- External compute routing must consider privacy, data residency, cost and authorization explicitly.
- Decisions must correlate workload ID, policy version, allocation, outcome and evidence without exposing sensitive prompts or user data.
- Green CI alone does not establish fairness, security or contract conformance.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory actual schedulers, resource managers, quotas, runtime limits and hardware adapters from repository paths.
2. Specify workload schema, units, priorities, quotas and error semantics.
3. Define and test admission control, reservations, leases and safe release.
4. Integrate CPU, memory, GPU/NPU, I/O, blockchain and Aurora through canonical interfaces.
5. Test concurrency, fairness, starvation, overload, restart, partitions and faulty providers.
6. Record full commit SHAs, source paths, test results, exit codes, logs and artifact hashes; classify unresolved gaps as `RESIDUAL`, `BLOCKED` or `UNRESOLVED`.

## Readiness checklist (0/12)

- [ ] Existing schedulers/resource managers inventoried.
- [ ] Canonical SSOT paths evidenced per resource domain.
- [ ] 170 planned contracts reconciled against the live catalog.
- [ ] Workload schema has concrete data types.
- [ ] Admission control and reservations specified.
- [ ] Quotas, fairness and starvation protection tested.
- [ ] CPU/GPU/NPU allocation validated.
- [ ] Isolation and capability boundaries tested.
- [ ] Aurora and blockchain resource contracts reconciled.
- [ ] Recovery, lease expiry and safe release tested.
- [ ] Complete Run/Job/Step evidence archived.
- [ ] Exact repository, commit, path and symbol references documented.

Checklist state is not proof of implementation or verification.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Compare all 170 planned contract IDs against the current catalog and report existing, missing, duplicate and unresolved entries with evidence.
2. Inventory existing canonical scheduling/resource functionality before proposing code changes.
3. Map every accepted function contract to exact repository, full commit SHA, path, symbol/blob and evidence, or document a reasoned exclusion/unresolved state.
4. Keep proposed standards distinct from registered normative standards.
5. Demonstrate admission, lease expiry, safe release, quotas, fairness, isolation and failure recovery with reproducible tests and artifacts.
6. Preserve SSOT boundaries and do not merge based on green CI alone.

**Current status:** architecture `PROPOSED`; catalog intake `NOT VERIFIED`; implementation `UNRESOLVED`. Issue creation itself does not prove catalog integration, implementation or CI verification.
